what_this_is: The D4a adjudication record. It is normative for the edges it adjudicates, and Confluence page 276594860 mirrors it. Guard G32 (MCP.Conformance.Adjudications) holds its rows equal to the views its sections bind, in both directions, with dispositions from the guard's closed set and every repository citation holding the bytes it quotes. A harness citation names the build by sha256 and a byte span. Gate 5 cannot read the build, so those citations are verified by the control's harness mode instead.

decision_row.why: R3 and R6 are the report's decision row. This record adds R1's broad half, which has a part per required _meta key (protocolVersion, clientCapabilities). The PO questions on MES-126 presented all three root causes, with R1 split as Q1a and Q1b.

stated_at.bytes:
**R3 and R6 are a DECISION row, not a fix row.** Both are documented SDK design decisions
that the referee contradicts — `dispatch.ex:146` names the missing version gate as the
design, and `dispatch.ex:66-68`/`:131-139` document `initialize → -32022` and why. PM ruling
(MES-24, comment 24503) routes them to the **release ticket as decisions requiring a PO
call**, *not* to MES-43 as gaps to fix. They are carried here so the measurement is not
lost and so **nobody schedules them as bugs**.

root_cause.narrower_than_this_evidence: R1 as the report words it names server/discover's missing _meta validation, over both required keys, protocolVersion and clientCapabilities. That is what the check SEES: at the accepted run, discover returned a normal result, hence got undefined. This edge is a different request, a tools/call. On every method other than server/discover the SDK answers a missing protocolVersion with -32022, because Meta.validate_protocol_version/2 returns {:error, :missing} and the gate maps every error to -32022; and it does not look at clientCapabilities at all, so a request missing only that key is served normally. The suite reads both cases as -32602 on every method (suite_required_keys). So R1 has a narrow half (discover validates _meta) and a broad half (which code a request missing a required key earns on every method), and each half has a part per key. The report routes the narrow half as a fix and states neither part of the broad half. The PO questions split them, Q1a for a missing _meta or protocolVersion and Q1b for a missing clientCapabilities, and the PO ruled both YES (MES-126 comment 29509).

gate.bytes:
defp handle_request(method, id, params, ctx, config) do
    meta = Meta.from_params(params)

    case Meta.validate_protocol_version(meta, target_version(config)) do
      :ok -> route(method, id, params, ctx, config)
      {:error, _} -> reply(id, Error.unsupported_protocol_version(meta.protocol_version), config)
    end

rows.rationale: The edge stands at the requirement: the check's description is method-general, the suite's own mock applies it to every method, and this claim asserts the opposite code. But the check never sends tools/call, so the view's evidence clause claiming the fixture is exactly this request shape is wrong about the method. This record recorded that as a finding, and did not edit the generated view. The narrow fix cannot land without deciding the broad question, because the SDK's own tests encode discover-without-_meta as a success (see if_conformance_fixed). The PO has ruled Q1a and Q1b YES (MES-126 comment 29509): a request missing either required key is answered -32602 on every method, server/discover included. So the disposition is fix_sdk, owned by MES-43 (comment 29510, the R1 / Q1a and R1 / Q1b bullets), and the tests if_conformance_fixed lists change in the same change, as measured_break_sets measures.

measured_break_sets.what: Which tests go red under each answer to Q1a and Q1b, measured rather than read. The SDK is not changed: a scratch copy of the branch had its dispatch gate patched to answer -32602 for a missing key, under six variants (below), and the full suite was run once per variant at seed 0. The one G32 citation_drift failure that the patch itself causes (the committed-tree audit) is excluded from every list. The patch is not committed; the close-out on MES-126 carries it.

variants.Q1a_yes: a missing _meta or protocolVersion earns -32602 on every method, server/discover included
variants.Q1b_yes: a missing clientCapabilities earns -32602 on every method, server/discover included

measured_break_sets.equalities_measured: Q1a_discover_only, Q1b_discover_only and Q1a_and_Q1b_discover_only redden the same set, every_discover_only_variant. Q1a_and_Q1b_yes reddens the same set as Q1b_yes, and Q1a_yes's set is contained in it.
measured_break_sets.why_q1b_is_wider: The test helpers that stamp _meta put protocolVersion in it and not clientCapabilities: dispatch_test.exs meta/1 and streamable_http_stateless_test.exs @meta are cited here. Every test built on such a helper passes the version gate today and would be refused under Q1b_yes.

rows.claim: a tools/call carrying no `params.name` emits NO `mcp-name` header, rather than an empty one

et_test.asserts: A tools/call whose params carry no name goes out with no mcp-name header at all.

check.requires: An Mcp-Name header on tools/call equal to params.name.

check_body.bytes: checkMcpNameHeader(e,t,n){let r=t.method;if(this.nameHeaderChecks.has(r))return;let i=n===`params.uri`?t.params?.uri:t.params?.name,a=e.headers[`mcp-name`],o=[];a?a!==i&&o.push(`Mcp-Name header value '${a}' does not match body ${n} '${i}'.`):o.push(`Missing Mcp-Name header on ${r} request. root_cause.why: With params.name absent, the check binds its expected value to undefined. If no header is sent, it pushes the missing-header error. If any header is sent, the raw comparison of a string against undefined is true, and it pushes the mismatch error. No client behaviour passes the check on this input. The check also records only the FIRST tools/call of a run (the nameHeaderChecks early return), so it runs green only because the fixture's first tools/call carries a name.

cause_slug.note: Confirmed, and sharpened: the check is not merely unexercised on this input, it has no passing answer on it. The input itself is schema-invalid, since name is required on a tools/call, so the defect is dormant for any well-formed request.

rows.rationale: Nothing in our tree changes. This is a SECOND suite defect, distinct from MES-124's raw comparison. MES-124's upstream report should carry it, and that is routed to the PM as a finding.

rows.member: MCP.Transport.StreamableHTTPStatelessTest/test tools/call input-required → retry with requestState → completion
rows.claim: that InputRequiredResult carries `inputRequests`, and the SDK puts that value on the wire as a JSON ARRAY

et_test.bytes:
test "tools/call input-required → retry with requestState → completion" do
    first = post(opts(), rpc("tools/call", with_meta(%{"name" => "needs_input"}))) |> result()
    assert first["resultType"] == "input_required"
    assert first["requestState"] == "rs-token-1"
    assert is_list(first["inputRequests"])
et_test.asserts: The InputRequiredResult the real plug returns carries inputRequests as a JSON array.

check.requires: Every message the implementation sent validates against the spec schema.

predicate.bytes: a.push({id:`wire-schema-valid`,name:`WireSchemaValid`,description:`Every JSON-RPC message the implementation sent is valid per the spec JSON schema for the negotiated spec version`,status:o.length===0?`SUCCESS`:`FAILURE`

schema_definition.bytes:
InputRequests:{additionalProperties:{$ref:`#/$defs/InputRequest`},description:`A map of server-initiated requests that the client must fulfill.
Keys are server-assigned identifiers; values are the request objects.`,type:`object`}
schema_definition.reading: InputRequests is an object whose additionalProperties are InputRequest. An array is not an object.

root_cause.why: MRTR.input_required/2 is spec'd list() | nil and passes the value through untouched, so a handler that follows the SDK's own type puts an array on the wire. The Sprint 4 register recorded this as a gap to fix (gap 7).

routed_as_a_fix.bytes: | 7 | `MRTR.input_required/2` typespec/doc say `list()`; the wire type is an object | C-A: the list form fails `wire-schema-valid` |

why_the_check_was_green.bytes:
* `MRTR.input_required/2` is spec'd `list() | nil` while the wire type
      `InputRequests` is a JSON **object** keyed by input name. This file sends
      a map, per the schema.

cause_slug.note: Confirmed: the accepted run only ever saw the conformance adapter, which sends a map per the schema. The SDK path that puts an array on the wire was never exercised by the harness.
